review_candidates.title: Senior Systems Engineer
review_candidates.description: Within NHS England, system engineering is about building in the whole-system space rather than specialising solely in applications, infrastructure, networks, or platforms. We are seeking experienced Senior Systems Engineers to join multidisciplinary product teams across a range of national services. You will play a key role in designing, building, operating, and continually improving systems that support citizens, patients, and healthcare professionals across England. As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will work on services used by millions of people. These range from citizen-facing digital products to critical back-end platforms and APIs. The role involves solving complex technical challenges and applying modern engineering practices to ensure systems are secure, reliable, resilient, and maintainable. We currently have opportunities across multiple teams, using a diverse range of technologies including Python, TypeScript, .NET, Terraform, AWS, and Azure. Alongside technical delivery, you will contribute to engineering best practices, support colleagues through mentoring and knowledge sharing, and help shape the direction of the services and platforms you work on. On-call Participation in a shared on-call rota may be required to support a 24/7/365 service, this rota covers evenings, weekends, and public holidays. As a Senior Systems Engineer, You Will Develop, build, and operate highly available, distributed systems that deliver critical national services within NHS England. Work within and contribute to NHS England's engineering principles and standards. Take technical ownership across the system landscape, including applications, infrastructure, networking, environments, CI/CD pipelines, and operational tooling. Collaborate with peers to solve complex technical challenges and drive continual improvement in engineering standards across the organisation. Contribute to the ongoing improvement of engineering maturity within the team. Coach, mentor, and support colleagues in their professional and technical development. Candidates must demonstrate experience of the following in their application: Application development Test engineering and automation Infrastructure engineering, e.g. infrastructure as code CI/CD including design, development and maintenance of pipelines Operating services in production NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS. Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms — enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services. In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department. If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR). This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process. Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices. Staff recruited from outside the NHS will usually be appointed at the bottom of the pay band. We cannot offer visa sponsorship for any vacancies. For further details / informal visits contact: Name: John Collinson Job title: Principal Systems Engineer Email address: john.collinson3@nhs.net

review_candidates.description: Network Operations Center (NOC) Engineer / Network Engineer Location: Omaha, NE (Onsite - 5 days a week) As a Network Operations Center (NOC) Engineer, you will support mission-critical network operations in a fully onsite, incident-management focused environment. You’ll monitor, troubleshoot, and help maintain network connectivity across routers, switches, core protocols, telecom/ISP services, and microwave radio communications. This role is ideal for a network professional who thrives in a fast-paced operations setting and is ready to support essential transportation, utility, telecom, or railroad systems. This is a fully onsite role with a fixed second or third shift schedule: 3:15 PM–11:15 PM, or 11:15 PM–7:15 AM The workweek will be either Sunday–Thursday or Tuesday–Saturday. Responsibilities Monitor and support network operations from a NOC environment, responding to incidents, alerts, outages, and service-impacting events. Perform troubleshooting for network connectivity, routing, switching, and core network protocol issues. Support configuration, administration, and maintenance activities for routers, switches, and related network infrastructure. Coordinate with telecom vendors, utility providers, ISPs, and internal teams to resolve circuit, connectivity, and service issues. Assist with microwave radio communication support, including initial triage and escalation; general familiarity is sufficient, and deeper technical knowledge can be developed on the job. Support incident management processes, including issue identification, prioritization, documentation, escalation, and resolution tracking. Use Linux system administration knowledge to support network-related systems and operational tools. Communicate clearly during active incidents, providing timely status updates to stakeholders and technical teams. Help maintain operational documentation, runbooks, incident records, and knowledge articles. Support mission-critical environments where reliability, responsiveness, and attention to detail are essential. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to restore services quickly and reduce recurring incidents. Participate in shift-based handoffs to ensure continuity across network operations. Qualifications Experience with general network administration, network configuration, and troubleshooting. Strong understanding of networking fundamentals, including routers, switches, and core network protocols. Experience working in a NOC, operations center, incident-management, or technical support environment. Familiarity with telecom vendor, ISP, WAN, or utility connectivity coordination. General familiarity with microwave radio communications; hands-on or deeper technical experience is a plus. Familiarity with Linux distributions and basic system administration concepts. Ability to assess incidents, troubleshoot under pressure, and escalate appropriately. Strong communication skills with the ability to coordinate across vendors, ISPs, technical teams, and stakeholders. Availability to work fully onsite on a fixed second or third shift schedule. Availability to work either a Sunday–Thursday or Tuesday–Saturday workweek. Preferred experience supporting railroad environments, train operations systems, Positive Train Control, or Centralized Traffic Control. Experience supporting other mission-critical transportation, utility, telecom, or infrastructure environments is highly valued. Strong sense of ownership, reliability, and follow-through in an operational support environment.
